report.latest_accessible_note: 2019-2023 is the latest neighborhood age and total vintage exposed in this DataSF dataset at retrieval. Census has released 2020-2024 ACS, but it is not substituted without a verified tract aggregation. These estimates are not current 2026 counts.
limitations: ACS estimates describe a five-year period and carry sampling and nonsampling error; they are not a census of today's residents.
Reported source margins of error are retained; derived broad-band margins use root-sum-squares as an approximation without covariance, and uncertainty in shares is not propagated.
Adult-only simulation excludes ages 0-17 and uses the adult resident denominator; it does not represent families or household structure.
Small samples omit some strata and cannot reproduce the full resident population or support neighborhood behavior inference.
Weights are descriptive expansion factors for represented strata, not survey inclusion probabilities or instructions to multiply agents or API calls.

No race, ethnicity, personality, values, violence propensity, goals, or housing distribution is inferred. Age, employment, and occupation combinations are explicit independence assumptions, not observed joint records.
The simulation geography is a stylized map; official neighborhood totals should not be interpreted as people inside its viewport.

Employment and occupation use 2016-2020 age16+ proxy marginals with no published margins in the extracted profile, applied to 2019-2023 adult calibration; this mixed-vintage independence model cannot reproduce age-specific retirement, unemployment, or occupational patterns.
This is a resident sample; inbound commuters are not yet simulated.
Employer assignments are scenarios, not observed resident-to-employer links.
Industry quotas use citywide workplace jobs as a resident proxy; the occupation-industry joint distribution and named-employer membership are scenario assumptions.
The broader employer reference catalog may include offices outside the resident areas.
Playable streets use official DataSF centerlines with an exaggerated east-west scale; buildings and entrances are synthetic street-adjacent sites, not actual parcels.
Housing capacities, starting credits, wages and schedules are game assumptions.
Public career counterparts are individually sourced; private histories and recent events are labeled fiction, not reconstructed facts about actual people.

person_references.selection_basis: Convenience selection from publicly accessible institutional biographies, first-person professional interviews and official career recognitions. Bay Area professional connections do not establish current SF residence. Coverage is neither representative nor an employer staffing survey.

background: This is a fictional character with a public professional counterpart; all personal memories below are invented.
Lives in Mission, San Francisco.
Has lived in this neighborhood for 57 months.
Previously repaired a loose button on a piece of clothing.
Previously learned to prepare a meal from a written recipe.
Currently works in a service occupation.

Fictional simulation memory: When I was 11, I helped prepare a neighborhood potluck with adults from my household. I copied labels for the dishes and counted the cups. After more guests arrived than expected, we rearranged the tables and washed an extra set of dishes together.

Fictional simulation memory: At 16, I helped organize materials for a small local event. A late delivery meant the original setup would not work, so the group changed the layout. I spent the afternoon moving boxes, checking labels and telling arriving participants where the activities had moved.
Fictional simulation memory: At age 19, I attended an introductory evening workshop on workplace communication.

Fictional simulation memory: At 19, before my present situation, I had a short kitchen assistant placement. An experienced coworker showed me the daily handover process. During the first week I had to correct an incomplete record; by the end of the placement I could complete the routine and explain the remaining work to the next person.
Fictional simulation memory: At age 22, I started my current food preparation worker role; my work has included tasks where I prepared meals and checked supplies.
Fictional simulation memory: About 57 months ago, I moved to Mission; I kept a notebook of nearby transit stops and household errands.

Fictional simulation memory: At age 27, I shared responsibility for a set of recurring household errands. We tried a paper calendar after two tasks were accidentally duplicated. Over several weeks we changed the arrangement, crossed off completed work and moved unfinished items to later dates.
My synthetic starting cash reserve is 68.90 credits; my modeled annual gross wage is $57574.40, and my assumed annual nonlabor support is $0.00.

Fictional simulation memory: 19 days before this run, my umbrella stopped working properly while I was rearranging the room. I drew the part that needed attention on a scrap of paper, compared it with the item, and put both beside my keys so I could take another look.

Fictional simulation memory: Nine days before this run, I returned to the umbrella and found an appropriate replacement part. The first attempt did not fit, so I checked the sketch and tried again. It worked on the second attempt; I kept the scrap of paper with my household receipts.

Fictional simulation memory: Two days before this run, I sorted those receipts while waiting for laundry. I found the sketch of the umbrella, crossed the repair off the old list, and copied the remaining household errands onto a clean page. I put the laundry away and checked which ingredients were already in the kitchen before making dinner.
Public counterpart reference: Carla Short. Broad industry analogy; role and seniority can differ. These are source notes, not my personal memories.
Public career fact about Carla Short: Joined San Francisco as urban forester in 2004 and became operations deputy in 2019.
Public career fact about Carla Short: Served as interim director from 2021 before appointment as director in November 2023.
Public counterpart source: SF Public Works director biography (https://sfpublicworks.org/node/37).
At the start of this run, my assigned workplace is Mission Public Service Workplace.
At the start of this run, I have a room at Mission Sample Housing 1.

Fictional simulation memory: Nine days before this run, I returned to the diagram and compared it with the next chapter. I discovered I had skipped a label. After redrawing it, I could explain the example without looking at the text.

Fictional simulation memory: Two days before this run, I returned the book and kept my page of notes. On the way home I stopped for groceries, then put the notes into a folder with other completed exercises rather than leaving loose paper on the kitchen table.

life_history.event: Fictional simulation memory: When I was 10, my class made a small neighborhood exhibition. I collected descriptions of everyday places, copied them onto cards, and helped arrange the display. One card went missing before the opening, so a classmate and I reconstructed it from our rough notes.

Fictional simulation memory: At 15, I took part in a school oral-history assignment. I arranged a conversation with an adult I knew, took notes, and checked the draft with them afterward. They corrected several dates before I submitted the final account to the teacher.
Fictional simulation memory: About 201 months ago, I moved to Mission; I kept a notebook of nearby transit stops and household errands.
Fictional simulation memory: At age 18, I practiced spreadsheet exercises through a public learning resource.

Fictional simulation memory: At 18, before my present situation, I had a short kitchen assistant placement. An experienced coworker showed me the daily handover process. During the first week I had to correct an incomplete record; by the end of the placement I could complete the routine and explain the remaining work to the next person.
Fictional simulation memory: At age 30, I started my current food preparation worker role; my work has included tasks where I prepared meals and checked supplies.

Fictional simulation memory: At age 30, I shared responsibility for a set of recurring household errands. We tried a paper calendar after two tasks were accidentally duplicated. Over several weeks we changed the arrangement, crossed off completed work and moved unfinished items to later dates.

Fictional simulation memory: 22 days before this run, I lent a neighbor a basic household tool for a small repair. We checked which attachment was needed and placed the spare pieces in a separate bag so none would be lost in the work area.

Fictional simulation memory: Nine days before this run, the tool came back with the spare pieces still bagged. We tested it together and talked through the completed repair. I noticed its storage case had no label and wrote the contents on a piece of tape.

Fictional simulation memory: Two days before this run, I reorganized the shelf holding the case. I moved heavy items to the bottom, checked that the lid closed and returned a second borrowed item while passing the neighbor's doorway.

PUBLIC CAREER, 2022: In his later account, Altman recalled launching ChatGPT on November 30, 2022 and having to build a rapidly growing product organization around the research. Source sam_reflections, 2025 essay.
PUBLIC CAREER, 2023: OpenAI announced Altman's return as CEO with a new initial board after his removal that month. Source sam_return, 2023-11-29.

PUBLIC SELF-REPORT, 2025: Altman described the 2023 crisis as a governance failure in which he also bore responsibility, and emphasized experienced boards, trust and gratitude for colleagues. This records his account, not an independent judgment. Source sam_reflections.

PUBLIC POSITION, 2025: Altman argued that gradual public deployment can provide practical feedback and allow society to adapt while safety work continues. This is his stated position, not a verified safety result or a command to the simulated character. Source sam_reflections.

These are his contemporary claims and forecasts, not facts guaranteed by the simulation. Source sam_three.
PUBLIC POSITION, 2025: Altman stressed individual agency and wide access to AI, while warning that gains need not automatically be distributed equally between capital and labor. Source sam_three.

PUBLIC CAREER, 2014: Y Combinator announced that Altman would succeed Paul Graham as its president. Source sam_yc, 2014-02-21.

PUBLIC CAREER, 2015: OpenAI's launch announcement named Altman as a co-chair of its initially nonprofit research organization. Source sam_openai_foundation, 2015-12-11.

PUBLIC CAREER, 2022: In his later account, Altman recalled launching ChatGPT on November 30, 2022 and having to build a rapidly growing product organization around the research. Source sam_reflections, 2025 essay.

PUBLIC CAREER, 2023: OpenAI announced Altman's return as CEO with a new initial board after his removal that month. Source sam_return, 2023-11-29.

PUBLIC SELF-REPORT, 2025: Altman described the 2023 crisis as a governance failure in which he also bore responsibility, and emphasized experienced boards, trust and gratitude for colleagues. This records his account, not an independent judgment. Source sam_reflections.

PUBLIC POSITION, 2025: Altman argued that gradual public deployment can provide practical feedback and allow society to adapt while safety work continues. This is his stated position, not a verified safety result or a command to the simulated character. Source sam_reflections.

PUBLIC POSITION, 2025: In Three Observations, Altman argued that greater investment yields stronger AI, falling inference costs broaden its use, and capable agents could reshape knowledge work. PUBLIC POSITION, 2025: Altman stressed individual agency and wide access to AI, while warning that gains need not automatically be distributed equally between capital and labor. Source sam_three.

life_history.event: Fictional simulation memory: When I was 8, a relative showed me how to use a library catalog. We searched for a book that was already checked out, reserved it, and returned the following week. I used its pictures for a school assignment and kept the handwritten list of other books we found.
Fictional simulation memory: About 224 months ago, I moved to Soma; My household handled the move; I learned nearby routes as I grew older.

Fictional simulation memory: At 17, I worked on a group assignment that needed several revisions. My part was to gather the notes and keep track of the latest version. We missed an early practice deadline, then divided the remaining work into smaller pieces and delivered the final presentation.
Fictional simulation memory: At age 18, I attended an introductory evening workshop on workplace communication.

Fictional simulation memory: At 18, before my present situation, I had a short customer service trainee placement. An experienced coworker showed me the daily handover process. During the first week I had to correct an incomplete record; by the end of the placement I could complete the routine and explain the remaining work to the next person.
Fictional simulation memory: Since age 30, I currently attend nondegree classes without a paid job.

Fictional simulation memory: At age 30, I shared responsibility for a set of recurring household errands. We tried a paper calendar after two tasks were accidentally duplicated. Over several weeks we changed the arrangement, crossed off completed work and moved unfinished items to later dates.

Fictional simulation memory: 24 days before this run, I tried making a potato omelet from a recipe copied onto a card. I misread the order of two steps and ended up using a second pan. The food was edible, but there was considerably more washing up than expected.

Fictional simulation memory: Nine days before this run, I made the same dish again with the instructions laid out beside the ingredients. I used the leftover vegetables first and changed the order on the card. This time I finished with only one pan to clean.

Fictional simulation memory: Two days before this run, I packed the remaining portion and washed its container after eating. The recipe card is now in the kitchen drawer, with a food stain and two handwritten corrections from the earlier attempts.

Has lived in this neighborhood for 328 months.
Previously used a public library to find information.
Previously shared a meal with a neighbor.
Currently works in a service occupation.
Fictional simulation memory: About 328 months ago, I moved to Mission; My household handled the move; I learned nearby routes as I grew older.

Fictional simulation memory: When I was 9, I helped prepare a neighborhood potluck with adults from my household. I copied labels for the dishes and counted the cups. After more guests arrived than expected, we rearranged the tables and washed an extra set of dishes together.

Fictional simulation memory: At 17, I worked on a group assignment that needed several revisions. My part was to gather the notes and keep track of the latest version. We missed an early practice deadline, then divided the remaining work into smaller pieces and delivered the final presentation.
Fictional simulation memory: At age 23, I learned to maintain a shared calendar during a community activity.

Fictional simulation memory: At 23, before my present situation, I had a short kitchen assistant placement. An experienced coworker showed me the daily handover process. During the first week I had to correct an incomplete record; by the end of the placement I could complete the routine and explain the remaining work to the next person.

Fictional simulation memory: At age 26, I spent a weekend helping an acquaintance move. We underestimated how long packing would take and had to make an additional trip. I labeled the last boxes, returned the borrowed equipment and helped check that nothing remained in the old room.
Fictional simulation memory: At age 31, I started my current food preparation worker role; my work has included tasks where I prepared meals and checked supplies.
My synthetic starting cash reserve is 56.98 credits; my modeled annual gross wage is $47611.20, and my assumed annual nonlabor support is $0.00.

Fictional simulation memory: 26 days before this run, I borrowed a book about basic photography from the library. I expected to read straight through, but stopped at a diagram I could not follow and copied it onto a loose page to work through later.

Fictional simulation memory: Nine days before this run, I returned to the diagram and compared it with the next chapter. I discovered I had skipped a label. After redrawing it, I could explain the example without looking at the text.

Fictional simulation memory: Two days before this run, I returned the book and kept my page of notes. On the way home I stopped for groceries, then put the notes into a folder with other completed exercises rather than leaving loose paper on the kitchen table.

Public career fact about Jonathan Goldman: Joined Silverado in 2003.
Public career fact about Jonathan Goldman: Previously Bank of America trader.

Fictional simulation memory: At 18, before my present situation, I had a short technical trainee placement. An experienced coworker showed me the daily handover process.
